## Details

### elektron-firmware-tool

C, MIT licence. Unpacks Elektron .syx firmware and repacks it as a valid file. Lists Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX among supported devices - currently the only Analog Heat-relevant tool we found. Forum listing: 113 stars, repo created 2026-07-22, "last commit 1 month ago" at the time of listing.

_Sources: forum mod list (mods.php?id=7), forum thread 8_

### Synthack-OS (Syntakt MAX 1.0, SY FM4 modular builder)

Several firmware mods in one build; SY FM4 included. Builder is a Windows app (a user asked for a web version). Needs the user's own OS 1.41.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): Upstream is Angelo-politek/Synthack-OS ("SyntHack OS", MIT, v0.9.0 on 2026-10-19: performance FX on all tracks replace beat repeat, quantized retrig, separate IN R page; v0.8.1 fixes boot crashes with sample projects; v0.8.0 adds the third send). This entry is the fork by karigardarsson, branded "Syntakt MAX": Modular Builder RC2 (2026-10-20) restores native MIDI parameter ownership for the third send, compressor and beat repeat; RC1 (2026-10-19) adds SY FM4 and per-feature selection; MAX 1.0 (2026-10-17) was a fixed seven-feature bundle. Brick-risk flag set on altstrument._

_Related: fork of `synthack-os-upstream` (GitHub fork flag); uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: tools/unpack wraps elektron-firmware-tool) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: forum threads 81 and 85, README (2026-11-11)_

### Syntakt Performance Mods (JOG page, PERFORM DJ filter)

Performance mods built from the user's own official Syntakt OS file: a desktop builder (Python/Tk, Windows launchers), a browser builder (the same builder ported to JavaScript, the firmware tool compiled to WebAssembly, byte-identical output in the tests) and an add-on that merges the mods into an existing Syntakt MAX manifest (the mod area grows to 128 KB; the code sits above MAX 1.0's 64 KB). The core (mod-area loader, splash, parameter hooks, MIDI id guard, master filter) comes from the SyntHack / Syntakt MAX line, the SY CHORD bank and Deja Vu from the Syntakt Firmware Workbench. A LiveLink CDJ bridge is shelved and not public. Marked experimental; ships no firmware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-17; README, STATUS and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES read (one public commit). 2026-11-18 (README, STATUS, USER_GUIDE): PERFORM's THRU is a true bypass since TEST37c (before, the whole mix kept running through the analog FX block and sounded harder and crackly on the author's unit, I139); TEST38 adds DRV, which overrides the FX block's DRIVE in the audio interrupt's copy of the live values with a glide and, at THRU, drives the mix without filtering it. Knob A needs 6 detents to cross the centre notch, about 126 detents a side.

_Related: builds on `synthack-os` (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES: core mods from SyntHack as integrated in Syntakt MAX; the add-on merges into a MAX manifest); vendors `syntakt-firmware-workbench` (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES: SY CHORD bank and Deja Vu from Firmware Workbench (MIT)); uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: the builder needs elektron-firmware-tool) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-17, README (2026-11-17), docs/STATUS.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, README, docs/STATUS.md, docs/USER_GUIDE.md (2026-11-18), altstrument (2026-11-17)_

### digikit

Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 2026-11-12 (b657f37, via altstrument): a USB take-over for fast sample transfer in the workbench with a read-back hash check per file, a diagnostic module that reads card information, a restructured SDK, fixes to the card image and the patch kit on Windows. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project. 2026-11-14 (finding 123 rewritten, findings 128-129, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ADDRMAP.md): the USB take-over is deleted (its commands answer E_STATE); core/usb-bulk-audio adds a vendor bulk OUT interface to the USB AUDIO/MIDI configuration at boot, so there is no mode switch (a probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads 3.38 MB/s on a DN2, 2.74 MB/s on a DT2). Runtime 0.7.0: modules declare machines and effects with builder calls and the runtime commits them at once or refuses; a module of another major.minor is refused (E_CONTRACT); the patched-in content macros are gone. An address map names code addresses in crash records and profiles; the debug module can keep a card log that survives a crash. Finding 128 (static): the SHARC hook sites cannot move into run-time services, because the ColdFire uploads the whole DSP image before the card is readable. 2026-11-15 (MODULE-AUTHORING, design/module-sdk, handover): modules no longer declare their DSP cycles; module:check measures the worst steady block and stores a per-voice or per-effect DSP cost in the package, and one shared rule (largest voice cost x voices + effect costs within the headroom) now runs in the boot planner, the menu, patchkit fit and the web Transfer tab, which refuses a selection over the limit ('DSP LOAD need > free'). Modules built for the old descriptor must be rebuilt. Runtime limits now listed: 512 KiB arena, 64 KiB per module, 8 machine rows, 3 FX slots, DSP area 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2). The SDK sample kernel has since landed (2026-11-16): the Shot machine fell from about 5,000 to about 2,450 (DT2) / 2,660 (DN2) emulator instructions a block, bit-identical. 2026-11-16 (findings 130 and 132, sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md, handovers; runtime 0.8.2, untagged): one generated DSP register contract for module code (clobber, keep, stack, never_write), checked by patchkit build but only as a warning so far; the fx, machines, samples and lfo services are separate crates, the step before loadable services; module DSP tests moved to a SHARC-only rig (about 45 s instead of about 21 min). Finding 103 was partly withdrawn: several values reported as measured on silicon came from probe instructions the old assembler had mis-encoded (see digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md). No new unit run in this period. 2026-11-17 (findings 133-135, plans usb-fast-batch, runtime-slimming, r12-8-sharc-stubs, digikit-hot-reload, handovers; runtime 0.8.3, untagged): a Fast USB speed round ran on a DN2 (OS 1.12) and a DT2 (OS 1.17) on 2026-11-16 with every file hash-checked: one store-table commit for up to 16 files, copy/write overlap and fewer +Drive steps per file took a sample pack from 2.42 to 3.56 MB/s (DN2) and 2.32 to 3.07 MB/s (DT2) and a 9.8 MB file to 4.37 / 4.13 MB/s; a cached USB receive was slower and was dropped. Finding 133 (static): the card takes one transfer at a time under global mutexes, so parallel writers cannot help. Services become separate .dks files bound to the user's own firmware at install (patchkit bind; bound files hold firmware bytes and are never committed): lfo.dks is merged, Transfer installs the services a module needs (both emulator-tested), fx.dks and machines.dks are on a branch. Hot reload is an active plan again (finding 135, static firmware facts), not built. Facts in devices/digitakt-2.md. 2026-11-18 (findings 136-141, devices/syntakt.toml, plan syntakt.md): Syntakt OS 1.42 support in the emulator only. The emulator runs MAIN and the second ColdFire (section 7) in lock step, with digital audio (analog tracks silent); patchkit builds a no-seal 1.42 image that changes only section 3 and refuses sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8; the runtime, menu, health and input adapters boot on the emulated 1.42 and load the debug module over emulated USB MIDI. Nothing has been flashed to a Syntakt. The DT2 and DN2 device files gained [protect] windows (hardware blocks a content module may not address; the packer refuses such a module) and [container] roles; the bulk OUT interface (core/usb-bulk-audio) is now in the default device image of both. 2026-11-18 (docs/PATCHING, MODULES, ARCHITECTURE, plans runtime-and-services and r12-8-sharc-stubs, port files): machines and effects are run-time modules only; patchkit now refuses a patch-time machine or effect row. The services machines.dks and fx.dks have landed: unbound files hold no firmware bytes, `patchkit bind` makes the stock tails from the user's own firmware, and Transfer installs the services a module needs (emulator example on DN2 1.12: machines.dks 29,718 bytes). The SHARC hook sites now jump through 16 slot words that a service fills (4 used). core/usb-bulk-audio (Fast USB beside USB audio) moved from a separate patch set into the default `device` and `device-introblank` sets on both devices. `patchkit pack` refuses a content module whose code or data holds an address inside a device's protected windows (flash controller, FPGA, peer buses). The DN2 OS 1.11 port file grew from 277 to 358 anchors (1.12: 359), adding the USB, card-driver, DSP voice and link anchors. No new unit run in these files. 2026-11-18 (findings 147-149, handover 2026-11-18, plans extension-model and port-file, MODULES, LFO module docs): runtime 0.9.0 refuses modules built for an older minor runtime version and duplicate keys in a boot selection; a new module kind lfo-shape (template and a first module, lfo_shapes_1, with seven 32-sample shapes; the service holds up to eight, as wave numbers 7 and up) and a core/lfo image adapter in every DT2 and DN2 patch set; content modules reload without a boot (refused while the transport plays); one port file per device and firmware, picked by the firmware hash, is planned. Findings 147-149 read the play state, the filter type and the LFO paths statically on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. All emulator or static; no new unit run. An open risk the plan lists: after the last SysEx block the workbench flash flow can report done while the unit still writes flash. 2026-11-20 (finding 150 new, findings 110 and 148 updated, device files, plans and design digikit-project, extension-model, INSTRUMENTATION): the module file limit (upload stage buffer) doubles to 128 KiB on DT2, DN2 and Syntakt. Finding 150 reads the stock machine and filter type setters and the KitActive wrapper the machine chooser calls; finding 110 adds checked hook sites for a planned project service (slot setter, save, save exit) and what each stock project path (new, delete, clear, paste, format, load, rename) does; finding 148 traces the SHARC filter dispatch (two jump tables bounded at 7). The planned project service keeps per-project digikit data in projects/<slot>-<name>.dkp files, written after a successful stock save and archived, never deleted, when a slot changes hands. A calibration fit turns emulator instruction counts into device cycles from paired profiles. All static or emulator; no new unit run. 2026-11-21 (findings 151-157, plans card-write-guard, track-manager, usb-winusb, syntakt "Hardware bring-up", PATCHING "Flashing a Syntakt"): Syntakt hardware sets. The patched 1.42 image was 32 KB over the 2 MiB upgrade limit, so a core adapter (peer-image) stores the second CPU's section 7 packed and unpacks and hash-checks it in MAIN before it is streamed; a `device-peer` image with only that adapter and the full `device` set boot on the maintainer's unit. The first full image hung at the logo because the Syntakt bootstrap stages MAIN at 0x40200000 (DT2/DN2 0x40400000) and its in-place unpack overran (I183); patchkit now keeps an 8 KiB margin and refuses less. DIGIKIT > MODULES froze the unit because core/ui used Digitakt II key ids (I181); the first store lay beyond the unit's 1.82 GiB card (I182) and is now fixed at 1-1.5 GiB, checked against the driver's capacity. A new adapter card-guard hooks the firmware's eMMC write and erase and refuses requests outside each writer's sectors (on for the Syntakt, emulator-tested), against a stock Data API write that trusts the host's size (SB35). Also: a key-event hook site and the stock View and NameView classes (finding 155) with a planned shortcuts service and a track-manager tool module (host tests only); a WinUSB descriptor hook for the Fast USB interface (built, not yet tested on Windows or a unit); a DN2 unit calibration showing device/emulator SHARC cost factors from 1.01 (ALU) to 2.69 (memory). The public site still does not offer the Syntakt. 2026-11-22 (finding 158, FINDINGS, plans runtime-contract-and-lifecycle and ledgers/device-test-inventory, PATCHING, TESTING, AGENTS): the repository was reorganised (runtime/, services/, image-modules/, ports/; content modules under modules/<kind>/<author>/<name>) and checked byte for byte with a manifest tool. Finding 158, a static survey on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12 read once, says the ColdFire main OS runs from writable DDR, so almost every hook site and firmware table could be installed by the runtime at load instead of being flashed; the firmware has no indirect-call dispatcher to reuse; on the SHARC no load-time path exists, so 30 voice and effect sites stay flashed. A new plan (one package lifecycle for modules and services) follows from it. A new size gate measured the stored container against the 2,096,640-byte cap: DT2 1.17 1,616,928 B, DN2 1.12 2,028,608 B, Syntakt 1.42 2,102,528 B (5,888 B over; the first planned fix loads the DIGIKIT menu from the card). An inventory lists 105 device-test files that run on emulated units; a smoke set of 8 runs on each of DT2 and DN2. No new unit run. 2026-11-23 (finding 159 new, FINDINGS, plans resident-core-and-system-package, rc2s-1-boundary-inventory, rc3-header-table-v4, observability, runtime-contract-and-lifecycle, device files, ARCHITECTURE, TESTING): finding 159 (static) says the Syntakt image size is bound by the bootstrap's in-place unpack, so the stored literal tail of MAIN is padding, not waste, and no packer setting can beat it. The planned fix splits the runtime into a flashed resident core (about 108 KB) and a system package (about 167 KB) loaded from the card, with a new core-only level. The lfo service now installs its hooks at load; core/lfo left the DT2 and DN2 images. Header table v4 will refuse all older module files. No new unit run.

No tag yet. 2026-11-13 (finding 126, finding 123 update, MODULE-AUTHORING): runtime 0.6.0 drops the old module contract (dkm_init, the Api table and slots): every module uses dk_module and named imports, and a .dkm built for the old contract is refused (E_CONTRACT), so modules must be rebuilt. New core adapter sdhc-large lets the stock card driver move up to 511 KiB per command instead of 64 KiB for buffers the runtime registers; measured upload speed levers on a DN2 (8 MB in about 1.9-2.2 s with all on, 3.0 s off) and none on the DT2; the USB take-over is off by default after a second failure on a unit (I80). 2026-11-10 (findings 118-119, 56fbc11): finding 119 reads a track's Sound parameter words through anchored functions (folded into devices/digitakt-2.md); new modules Overdrive curves and TB303; a public site (https://eleklabs.github.io/digikit/) patches the stock .syx in the browser, flashes over USB and installs modules; the README still does not call the bootstrap-menu recovery tested. 2026-11-14 (later): runtime contract 0.8.0 replaces the .dkm keys table with a tagged header table, so every runtime-0.7 module must be rebuilt; a boot planner gives each selected module a verdict before anything loads; modules can add generic records; a DSP link queue gives every request an owner (closes finding 129's shared-result bug); the firmware hooks moved into a core platform adapter; a DSP planning budget per device (common page); the address names in the Log pane work on the device path only in the emulator so far. 2026-11-21 (altstrument, main @ 4e09d74 of 2026-11-20): a calibration runner and a Calibration tab in the Profile pane, a DSP_SWEEP log event (runtime 0.10), a SETUP command in the debug module, MIDI output to a target or the emulator; a machine whose module is absent reads MISSING and plays silence._

### SyntHack OS (upstream)

Unofficial modular patch set for the Syntakt: master compressor (THR/ATK/REL/MUP/RAT with meter, saved per pattern or global), dual-mono external input levels, boot splash, readable parameter values (Hz, dB, ms, %), beat repeat (v0.6.0), third send FX SND3 into chorus/flanger/phaser/crusher (v0.8.0). Mod area: 64 KB RAM, stored compressed and unpacked at boot. Each mods/<name>/patch.json lists the patch location, a hash of the expected original bytes and the new bytes; tools/build/build.py refuses the wrong OS, overlapping patches and protected sections. tools/emu is a ColdFire emulator (Unicorn + EMAC model); every mod is tested there before flashing. A git hook (tools/hooks) blocks firmware files from commits - a practice worth copying. README: seven mods running on real hardware (v0.8.0); RECOVERY.md exists. Planned: PIN lock, new LFO shapes, 3rd LFO/mod matrix, arpeggiator, resampling, new machines (RISER/DOWNFILTER, SY SWARM+), web builder. MIT, 66 commits, 9 stars. Brick-risk flag set on altstrument. Fork "Syntakt MAX" is the synthack-os entry.

### syntakt-machine45-research

Documentation, a C header and tools/check_stock_metadata.py (standard-library only; checks exact input hashes and selected metadata of the user's own extracted MAIN and section-7 files) for adding a separate 46th Machine with public ID 45 while keeping stock IDs 0-44. Claims: a distinct MAIN raw ID 45 and menu/metadata edits confirmed by static analysis; mapping of public ID 45 to compact selector 45 and implementation family e12 "strongly supported"; entering/leaving the machine, Sound-lock precedence and the p-lock lifecycle not verified end-to-end; arbitrary native DSP installation blocked/unproven; docs/DSP_ABI.md describes eight raw controls. Explicitly makes no claim of a hardware-working new Machine; the original private candidate is frozen. Files: MACHINE45_TECHNICAL_HANDOFF.md, EVIDENCE_INDEX.md (refers to a private 803-file census), docs/FROZEN_BASELINE.md, docs/PUBLICATION_POLICY.md. Excludes firmware images, opcode/disassembly dumps, coefficient tables, binary diffs and deployable packages. MIT. Meant to complement SyntHack OS and SY FM4 (FM4 extends machine 4; this concerns ID 45).

### Elektron Emu

Five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) that run each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU: Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles. Firmware not included; the user places the .syx from Elektron's site in a per-machine folder. +Drive emulated and persisted; WAV loading on DT2, Rytm and DN2. Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler, else a slow interpreter that renders offline only). ### Synfact

Mod system for the Syntakt bringing Digitakt mk1 sample machines (ONE SHOT, WERP, REPITCH, SLICE), a per-project sample pool with long samples in slots 65-128 and a basic sample manager. Experimental. MIT. 18 stars at first sight. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-02; README start read. 2026-11-02: the GitHub repo no longer answers (deleted, renamed or private); details here are from the earlier read. 2026-11-03: the Lapin list links it as an external web app, https://synfact.app (builds custom Syntakt firmware from the user's stock OS file). 2026-11-03: the project moved to GSM1980/synfact-dev and was rebuilt on elekloader (GPL-2.0; the old release repo was MIT): a core (mods/core-st) with hook bus, UI and SETTINGS events, SMZ4 banks of machines and modules that can change without reinstalling, long-sample storage (HZFS) and a project sample pool. Mods: SP sample machines, SY FM DTONE, audio recorder, third LFO, arpeggiator, POLY, system info, sample manager. Builds change MAIN and a bounded part of AUDIO only; a recovery core that never loads the bank can replace a bank that stops the unit from starting. Also builds in the browser (synfact.app). A snapshot of the old release repo survives as nrdsrfr/synfact-release (2026-10-17). 2026-11-06: project lifecycle audit after a user report of slow project load and save; arp-st leaves default carriers absent (81 % fewer emulated instructions); RANDOMIZE pages documented. 2026-11-09: new docs SETUP, MACHINES (writing a machine), MACHINE-REFERENCE and SAFE-BOOT- SMZ4-07-16; a safe-boot trial crashed every boot until core 1.7.1 (I62); a companion window broke BASE/WDTH until 1.7.2 (I63). 2026-11-14: a MAIN-CPU optimisation release across core and optional mods (full bank 86 % -> 83 % MAIN on a stock pattern); a withdrawn development core of the same number crashed every boot because a routine sat in boot storage that startup wipes (I104); LFO3 1.3 fully suspends an engine with neutral depth or no valid destination, which can change active RANDOM sequences; samplers' stereo code borrows the Chorus SRAM windows when Chorus is absent. 2026-11-17: new playhead-st 1.0 (per-track step order, saved in a free tail of each kit slot that stock never reads); Chorus 1.2 (assembly, bit-identical buses); core 1.8.2 fixes a stock deferred view cleanup that drops a close raised during UI composition, which left ARP blank after mute on the owner's unit (ARP 1.9.1-1.10.4 reports); core 1.9.0 (host API 15) lets Recorder 1.4 run MAIN reduced (mixer, FX and modulation skipped) while a finished take is edited, and speeds MAIN LR stereo capture (owner's unit: 92 % MAIN in PLAY, 99 % recording before); new docs RECORDER-AUDIO-PAUSE and RECORDER-CAPTURE-CPU are in Spanish. 2026-11-18 (docs/OS142-PORT.md, STOCK-SAMPLE-CORE-OVERLAP.md, mod CHANGELOGs): source builds now target Syntakt OS 1.42 (core 2.0.0; all 108 resident patch sites re-audited; no single code offset between 1.41 and 1.42). Core 2.0 requires SMZ4 feature 16 and contract 0x53594605 and refuses older and untagged banks, so every bank must be rebuilt. Core 2.0.1 fixes a boot crash with many stock samples: stock's sample blob in MAIN grew over Synfact's resident core at 0x46000000 (I145); the core now streams stock samples to the voice CPU page by page and draws waveforms only when a page asks. The web builder and SMZ catalogue are not yet on 1.42. 2026-11-18, later (docs/INTEGRATING.md, SYNFACT-WEB.md, js/README.md): the documented web core route now takes Syntakt OS 1.42; the normal build has ten optional groups (Playhead added; ARP needs LFO3) plus the always-on modulation skip, 768 selections the matrix checks against the reference build. 2026-11-19 (MACHINE-REFERENCE, FORMAT, TESTS, ADAPTING, mod READMEs and CHANGELOGs): core 2.0.3 (chorus-st now needs it), arp-st 1.10.7, playhead-st 1.1-1.2.1 with four new modes and a modal selector drawn through the native Bitmap API; playhead now builds before the other UI modules so its modal takes keys first. The OS 1.42 suite checks 218 stock preimages. Synfact names firmware routines by their OS 1.41 address even in 1.42 modules; only the newly named 1.42 addresses are 1.42. All new work emulator only. 2026-11-20 (new docs AUDIO-MEMORY-MAP, LFO3-MODULE-ONLY-INVESTIGATION, PROJECT-OPERATIONS-CPU, STOCK-MAIN-CPU-PROFILE in Spanish; new mods icache-lock-st and mix-fast-st; high-memory probe; core-st README, SAMPLE-POOL, SMZ4, mod CHANGELOGs): core 2.1.0 stops the sequencer and runs MAIN's reduced audio path while a native project worker (new, save, load, rename, copy, paste, clear, delete) runs, without the recorder. 2.1.1 frees the bank file's AUDIO section from MAIN's heap after boot (it stayed until reboot: 108,640 bytes in the normal bank, 711,152 with the MD machine) and compiles cold core files at -Os, so the 64 KiB resident reserve goes from 176 to 11,616 bytes free. 2.1.2 fixes a module-only bank (LFO3, ARP, zero machines): the registry never became active, so LFO3's page showed ERR labels; confirmed on the owner's unit. 2.2.0 grows the bank's AUDIO section to 4 MiB and moves the sample pool above AUDIO's own page (63.62 MiB of long samples, 31.30 before); new contract 0x53594606, so every bank must be rebuilt. 2.3.0 checks that a whole sample batch fits before changing AUDIO (AUDIO FULL), and Sample Manager 1.3 shows sizes and a project memory meter. New always-in-bank modules: mix-fast-st (skips zero gain ramps in the stock mix kernels, exact) and icache-lock-st (locks hot stock audio code in half of MAIN's I-cache); both CPU savings are models, pending the unit. An emulator profile of stock 1.42 says about half of MAIN's cost is instruction-cache misses. A test-only probe machine (type 70) checks on the unit that nothing writes the new high AUDIO zone and measures the AUDIO stack depth; no result yet. 2026-11-21 (new comp-st README, FX-BUS-COMPRESSOR-FEASIBILITY in Spanish, REAL-SYSTEM-PROFILE; ADAPTING, FORMAT, MACHINE-REFERENCE, SMZ4, mod CHANGELOGs, commits of 2026-11-20): new comp-st 0.2.0, a compressor on the FX track bus only. Its DSP is SyntHack OS's master-comp (MIT, kept in upstream/); the controls come from the user's own Digitakt OS 1.54 file. Detector on the FX ADC pair, gain through the two FX VCAs, parallel MIX; settings in the kit slot tail [0x15d0, 0x15e0). Core 2.4.0 (host API 16) adds event 15 FX_CV and takes over the shared Kit sites from Chorus 1.2.2 and LFO3 1.3.2; older cores reject such a bank. The owner reports comp-st 0.2.0 working on the unit. An emulator profile of the full shipped bank found that the mods are not an I-cache miss source; the stock audio block is, so a better lock set cannot win much. 2026-11-23 (new COMP-SIDECHAIN-FILTER-FEASIBILITY in Spanish; comp-st, core-st and samplers-st READMEs, mod.json and CHANGELOGs; MACHINE-REFERENCE, ADAPTING, TESTS): comp-st 1.0.0 is COMP's first release: a high-pass on the detector only (SCF: off plus 127 cutoffs, 60 Hz to 1 kHz), ATK and REL in ms, THR 127 by default. On the unit MAIN rose with 0.2.0's COMP page open; the GR meter's repaints were the cause, now capped at 10 Hz (I196). Core 2.5.0 lets samplers-st 1.6.0 run a stereo track's right channel inside the stock chain; emulator only.

### trig-seedr

Offline pattern algorithms as an elekloader mod, opened as a third TRIG page after EUCLIDEAN: generate rhythms, notes, accents, trig conditions, retrigs and sample locks for a track, audition takes with undo, apply groove timing and velocity, and rotate a track or the whole pattern. Everything it writes is ordinary pattern data that plays and saves on a stock OS. Analog Four MKII and Syntakt are planned. Groove tables can be made from the user's own Ableton Live grooves; none are shipped. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README and firmware notes read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-16 (v0.4.0/v0.4.1, README 0.5): navigation is LEFT/RIGHT, PAGE and the TRIG keys stay stock's while the page is open. 0.4.1 is the build to flash: 0.4.0 wrote new trigs without the stock SYN/SMP/ENV flag bits, and a compiler optimisation (store merging in m68k-elf-gcc 16.2) broke a step move in the emulator (I112). Recipes live in RAM only and are lost at power-off or a pattern change. The MAP source copies Grids' drum map (GPL-3.0, Mutable Instruments, not catalogued). 2026-11-17 (v0.5.0-v0.7.0, README, release notes, flashing, testing, firmware notes): first hardware passes on a Rytm MKII (0.5.1, 0.6.0). Since 0.5.1 YES writes a take only with grid recording on and a take stays only after FUNC + YES; changing track or pattern, closing or turning RECORD off restores the original. Fuzzing found that two lock lanes on one parameter lost locks (the Rytm keeps one lock per parameter and step); refused since 0.6.0. The mod is 62 KB of code and 107 KB of RAM. Planned after 1.0: a TURING page that rewrites the track at each loop end. 2026-11-18 (v0.7.1, README, manual, flashing, testing, status M2.6): 0.7 is declared a beta for users; feedback decides what changes before 1.0. 0.7.1 fixes YOLO: take() fell off its end without a return value, so whether a roll stayed depended on a leftover register; the emulator passed by chance (I142). The mod now builds with -Werror=return-type. Boot screen shows T071 (a patch release shows Txyz, a minor one TSxy). 2026-11-20 (README, docs/firmware-notes-st142.md, flashing-st.md, plan-syntakt.md, status S0.2-U3, mods/*-st, manual): a Syntakt OS 1.42 port is in development, tested in analog-emu only (102 emulator checks), with no file offered to flash; the beta stays Rytm-only, so `devices` stays analog-rytm. The mod's code is split into a device-neutral frame/ and one part per device. On the Syntakt it uses a minimal hook-bus core of its own (456 bytes, from Synfact's GPL sources) because Synfact's core-st 2.0.3 does not link with gcc 16.2, so it does not run beside Synfact's mods. Code and data sit at 0x47a00000-0x47b00000, a range the emulator never saw the OS use; a canary mod is to check that on a unit with all 64 sample slots loaded. Differences from the Rytm: no retrigs, accent or slide; NOTE only (chord notes kept); LOCK lists the track's machine's controls; no lock-row limit. The unit file is stock 1.42 rebuilt by elektron-firmware-tool with only MAIN changed. A device header (st_params.h) is generated from the user's own stock file and never committed. Unit steps planned: practise the startup-menu recovery, flash a round-tripped stock file, the canary, then the mod. Rytm manual: YES + SCENE does not save a pattern while the mod is open (the mod takes YES, SCENE closes it). 2026-11-21 (v0.8.0, README, release-0.8, flashing-st, testing, requirements, adding-a-device, site device pages): 0.8.0 makes the Syntakt (OS 1.42) a second device, "ready for testing" (beta), so `devices` now lists it. Its first hardware pass (2026-11-19, one unit, on the 0.7.1-labelled build of the same code) went in steps: the startup-menu way back on stock, a stock file round-tripped by elektron-firmware-tool, a memory canary over 0x478b0000-0x47bf0000 with all 64 sample slots loaded (OK), then the 15 first checks, including a take kept across a power off (I184). The Rytm build of 0.8.0 is the same instrument on reorganised code and has no unit pass yet. Analog Four MKII and Digitone II are named as the next devices (docs/adding-a-device.md).

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: an elekloader mod on core-ar2 0.13); uses tool `analog-emu` (README: tested in trigcondition/analog-emu); cites `libanalogrytm` (firmware notes: pattern.h as a source); builds on `synfact` (release-0.8: the Syntakt core's hook bus and elekloader's Syntakt profile come from synfact-dev); uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (release-0.8: repacks the Syntakt unit file) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Syntakt custom firmware (DelayCtrl, DJ filter, Drive rectifier)

Unofficial Syntakt OS 1.41 mods built on SyntHack OS: DelayCtrl turns MOD B into an Octatrack-style freeze and beat repeat that takes over the delay while it is selected; a DJ filter replaces LP-Notch in the FX filter's TYPE list; a rectifier is mixed into the FX Drive above 5 (digital tracks only); the FX SYN page holds reverb, filter and send controls. The repo keeps source and patch data only; a browser page or a Python build patches the user's own Syntakt_OS1.41.syx and publishes the expected SHA-256 of each build. It also carries a mod SDK (slot map, taken-spot list), a .sypatch.json patch format with a conflict checker, a Unicorn ColdFire harness and a pre-commit guard against firmware files; the browser build uses synfact-dev's engine (GPL-3.0-or-later) at a pinned commit, not vendored. RECOVERY.md: the bootstrap (section 2) is never touched, recovery is the DIN MIDI startup menu (FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4). 12 commits, all by the author, created 2026-11-22; not a GitHub fork (it imports SyntHack's mods with their MIT licence). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23.

_Related: builds on `synthack-os-upstream` (README and PROJECT_STATUS: built on SyntHack-OS by Angelo-politek; upstream SyntHack mods in mods/); uses tool `synfact` (README: the browser build needs synfact-dev js/src at a pinned commit, never vendored) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-23, README, MANUAL, PROJECT_STATUS, RECOVERY, LICENSE (2026-11-23)_

### SynPat (Syntakt pattern manager)

Unofficial tool that copies patterns (with their kits) between Syntakt projects, including across project format versions, and backs up and loads projects over USB MIDI. A Python codec for the .stprj project file (container, LZ4 blocks, layout) with a command line (info, verify round trip, copy) and a local web GUI that talks to the unit through WebMIDI and Elektron's RPC; runs in Docker. No README and no licence file; four commits on 2026-11-22 by the author, who also publishes the synfact release copy. Changes no firmware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-23.

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-23, stprj/cli.py, web/static/index.html, commit log (2026-11-23)_
